references.text: Describes how the righteous will flourish like a tree, similar to how the mustard seed grows into a tree where birds can rest.
Speaks of the righteous flourishing like palm trees and growing like cedars in Lebanon, parallel to the growth of the mustard seed.
Similar to how a small mustard seed grows into a tree, this passage describes how God will plant a small tree that will grow and provide shelter.
Micah's vision of nations sitting under their own vine and fig tree without fear may remind one of the birds finding rest in the mustard seed's tree.
Describes the Lord's house established on mountain tops and lifted above the hills, parallel to the idea of growth and significance found in the mustard seed parable.
Luke's version of the mustard seed parable, emphasizing how God's kingdom grows from small beginnings.
Mark's version of the mustard seed parable, which also highlights the growth from a small seed into a large tree.
